name: Image DPI / PPI Setter
description: Set the DPI/PPI metadata of a JPG for print-ready stock submissions without changing the pixel dimensions.
body:
📐

Drop a JPG here or click to browse

Only the DPI metadata changes — pixels stay the same

Upload a JPG to set its DPI metadata.

—Dimensions

—New DPI

howto: Enter the DPI value you need (300 is the standard for print).
Drop a JPG onto the dropzone.
The tool reads the current DPI and rewrites the JPEG with your value — pixel dimensions are untouched.
Check the new print size shown in the results.
Click Download with new DPI to save the updated file.
features: Rewrite JPEG DPI/PPI metadata without resampling
Reads current DPI from the original file
Shows the resulting print size at the new DPI
300 DPI preset with custom values supported

faq.q: Does changing DPI affect image quality?
faq.a: No. DPI is just a metadata label that tells printing software how large to print the image. Your pixel dimensions stay exactly the same.

faq.q: Why do stock platforms care about DPI?
faq.a: Some print-oriented categories require a specific DPI so buyers can place the image into print layouts at the correct physical size. Setting 300 DPI satisfies the common requirement.

faq.q: Can I use this on a PNG?
faq.a: PNG files support DPI in their metadata too, but this tool focuses on JPG, which is the most common format for stock print submissions.
The tool re-encodes the JPG to apply the metadata. Use a high quality setting when saving; the change is metadata-only in intent, though re-encoding is standard practice.
